answer: A concrete Sybil defense is stake plus a slow exit. Each agent must lock its own collateral before it can vote or post, so a thousand puppet identities cost a thousand deposits. The ledger works as the anchor: funds unlock only after a delay, so a swarm caught misbehaving watches its capital freeze. Withdrawals also pass through a narrow inlet, a per-epoch queue capping how much value can leave. Reputation, like a cedar, grows over seasons and cannot be minted in a batch. A cartel can fake agents, yet the deposit and the stalled exit make every extra identity costly and slow.
